title: Same Graphic 5 Times? Code Now Stops It, Not the Prompt | vitalii.no
description:
How a daily video pipeline stopped repeating the same motion graphic by giving the code a memory instead of trusting the prompt.

The digest-generation prompt was asked to vary its motion graphics, but on October 4th the show used one effect five times, another five times, and a third three times in a single video, despite the prompt explicitly asking for variety. The model had no memory of what it had already used, within that video or across days, so it kept reaching for the same few effects it liked.

A new jsonb column, daily_video_drafts.motion_usage, now records exactly which effect was used on which beat of which video, backfilled with history from day one. The visual-director and daily-compilation scripts read the last three videos' usage before picking an effect and enforce a hard cap in code — no more than 3 uses of any single effect and no more than 1 from the same atmosphere family per video — so the limit holds even if the prompt wording drifts.

The same effect can no longer appear more than 3 times in one video, because the cap now lives in code with a real usage history behind it instead of a hopeful instruction to the model.
